Includes unit tests.",

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement a new YARN module deployer as an implementation of the existing Spring Cloud Data (s-c-d) deployer SPI, plugged into the xd-admin orchestration layer, rather than modifying the core admin server.

Stage all deployment artifacts (application JARs, module JARs, configuration files) into HDFS under a versioned application directory, with a manifest file (properties/YAML) describing the modules, their artifacts, target app instances, and resource requirements; xd-admin reads/writes this manifest to orchestrate deployments (U1).

Integrate with YARN via the ResourceManager REST API (ws/v1/cluster/apps) for application submission, monitoring, and kill operations; each YARN application is tagged with appType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app, and modules are grouped into applications according to the manifest (U2).

Support multiple app instances through deployment properties using the pattern 'module.<moduleName>.yarn.app.*' with wildcard support ('module.*.yarn.app.*') resolved via relaxed property binding; per-instance settings include YARN queue, priority, memory, and CPU (U3).

Make deploy/undeploy operations asynchronous by enqueueing them as tasks executed by a background executor inside the deployer; the shell returns immediately after enqueueing, and deployment state is tracked and queryable via the ResourceManager REST API (U4).

Base module launching on Spring Boot's JarLauncher/PropertiesLauncher API: refactor the existing custom ModuleLauncher into a thin adapter over Boot's launcher, removing duplicated classpath/archive-handling logic (U6).

Resolve external module dependencies (JARs) from a repository (Maven coordinates or a shared HDFS lib directory) and add them to the Boot loader classpath (e.g., via loader.path or a custom LaunchedURLClassLoader arrangement) as the uniform mechanism for consuming external libraries (U5, U8).
Target Java 17, Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3 line, and Apache Hadoop 3.x client libraries, consistent with the stated Spring Framework 6.0 baseline.
Use Hadoop MiniYARNCluster/MiniDFSCluster for automated integration tests to avoid requiring a full cluster in CI.
assumptions: The existing s-c-d codebase (admin server, shell, deployer SPI, module registry) already exists; this increment adds the YARN deployer, manifest handling, and the launcher refactoring only.
A development/test YARN cluster with HDFS and the ResourceManager REST API enabled is available for manual and end-to-end verification.
A single experienced developer (familiar with Spring and Hadoop YARN) performs all work; 1 workday = 8 hours of focused development effort.
Unit tests for new code are included within each activity's estimate; a dedicated integration/system testing activity is estimated separately.
The deployment manifest format does not exist yet and its design is included in the U1 activity.
U5 is a time-boxed technical spike (prototype/proof-of-concept) whose findings feed into U6-U8; production-quality implementation of external library support is estimated under U8.
Documentation scope is limited to developer/reference documentation and test cases for JAR resolution (U7) plus minimal updates to user-facing deployer documentation.
Out-of-the-box (OOTB) modules themselves do not require modification; only verification that they can consume external libraries via the new mechanism.
No performance/load testing, security hardening (e.g., Kerberos), or HA work is in scope beyond basic functionality.
